schema: Editorial notes merged into `profitdecoded.js calendar` output, keyed by topic id. Only entries marked verified: true rest on a checked research dossier. Every other thesis and hook is a HYPOTHESIS: no figure, date or claim may reach a script until the topic's dossier passes the research gate. Titles avoid the 'How X Makes Money' template.

hbm-073-how-gift-cards-make-money-for-re.workingTitle: Billions Sit on Unused Gift Cards. Who Keeps the Money?
hbm-073-how-gift-cards-make-money-for-re.centralHook: Somewhere in a drawer, there's a gift card with money still on it. If it's never spent, who ends up with that money?
hbm-073-how-gift-cards-make-money-for-re.thesis: An unused balance on a non-expiring card stays spendable, but issuers estimate from their own history how much will not be redeemed and book that share as revenue gradually; unclaimed-property laws may send part to government agencies; federal rules block the quickest ways of taking it (verified dossier hbm-073).
hbm-073-how-gift-cards-make-money-for-re.audience: US adults who give or hold gift cards; holiday shoppers
primarySources: Starbucks FY2025 10-K
Darden FY2026 10-K
CFPB Regulation E gift-card rule
Bankrate/YouGov 2024 survey
hbm-073-how-gift-cards-make-money-for-re.factualRisk: Low (dossier verified; arithmetic checked; attribution rules in place)
hbm-073-how-gift-cards-make-money-for-re.visualPlan: Card balance counters, filing excerpts, money-flow of breakage, three-claimant comparison panel
hbm-073-how-gift-cards-make-money-for-re.status: Script exists (session-written, gates passed except packaging + one heuristic opening reading); timed for the holiday gift-card season

hbm-175-how-energy-drinks-make-money.workingTitle: Why an Energy Drink Company Spends Like a Media Company
hbm-175-how-energy-drinks-make-money.centralHook: One energy drink brand owns sports teams, events and a media house. What is it actually selling?
hbm-175-how-energy-drinks-make-money.thesis: HYPOTHESIS: leading energy drink brands earn their margin on brand and distribution rather than manufacturing; the public-company case (outsourced production, bottler distribution) can be documented from filings, the private one only from its own releases.
hbm-175-how-energy-drinks-make-money.audience: US adults 18-44; sports and gaming viewers
primarySources: Monster Beverage 10-K (manufacturing, distribution agreements, segment results)
Red Bull GmbH annual sales releases (private: company statements only)
hbm-175-how-energy-drinks-make-money.factualRisk: Medium: the private company's finances are self-reported; keep claims to what each source states
hbm-175-how-energy-drinks-make-money.visualPlan: Can-cost breakdown, distribution map, sponsorship timeline, filing excerpts

se-024-why-rolex-watches-appreciate.workingTitle: Why a Used Watch Can Cost More Than a New One
se-024-why-rolex-watches-appreciate.centralHook: Walk into a dealer and the watch you want isn't available. Walk across the street and it is, for more. Why?
se-024-why-rolex-watches-appreciate.thesis: HYPOTHESIS: controlled supply, allocation lists and a secondary market create prices above retail; how far this holds today must be checked against current market data.
se-024-why-rolex-watches-appreciate.audience: US adults 25-54 interested in luxury, collecting and investing
primarySources: Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry export statistics
Brand statements on production and authorised dealers
Secondary-market price indices (secondary source: label as such)
se-024-why-rolex-watches-appreciate.factualRisk: High: private company, no filings; price claims move quickly; avoid naming prices without dated sources
se-024-why-rolex-watches-appreciate.visualPlan: Retail vs secondary price chart (dated), supply funnel, dealer-allocation diagram
se-024-why-rolex-watches-appreciate.risk: If the research gate cannot reach two primary sources, promote the backup

pp-037-why-costcos-food-court-hot-dog-ne.workingTitle: Why Costco Won't Touch the Price of Its Hot Dog
pp-037-why-costcos-food-court-hot-dog-ne.centralHook: The cheapest thing at Costco may be the most strategic. Why would a company refuse to raise one price for decades?
pp-037-why-costcos-food-court-hot-dog-ne.thesis: HYPOTHESIS: the food-court price works as a signal of value that supports the membership model; Costco's own filings show how much of its operating income comes from membership fees (cs-001 dossier has a verified claim on this).
pp-037-why-costcos-food-court-hot-dog-ne.audience: US Costco shoppers and members; adults 25-64
primarySources: Costco FY2025 10-K (membership fees, operating income) - partly verified in dossier cs-001
Costco executive statements on the food-court price (dated, attributed)
pp-037-why-costcos-food-court-hot-dog-ne.factualRisk: Medium: price-history claims need dated sources; keep loss/profit claims to what Costco states
pp-037-why-costcos-food-court-hot-dog-ne.visualPlan: Price-over-time line, membership-fee vs operating-income bars, store-traffic diagram

hbm-129-how-ikea-makes-money-from-meatba.centralHook: A furniture company sells millions of meatballs. Is the restaurant really about food?
hbm-129-how-ikea-makes-money-from-meatba.thesis: HYPOTHESIS: food service and small add-on items keep visitors in the store longer and raise what they spend; the size of the food business can be sourced from the group's own reporting.
hbm-129-how-ikea-makes-money-from-meatba.audience: US adults who shop at IKEA; home and design viewers
primarySources: Ingka Group / Inter IKEA annual summaries (food revenue, visits)
IKEA store-layout statements and patents where public
hbm-129-how-ikea-makes-money-from-meatba.factualRisk: Medium: 'keeps shoppers longer' needs a documented source, not assumption
hbm-129-how-ikea-makes-money-from-meatba.visualPlan: Store floor-plan path, food revenue chart, basket diagram

hbm-031-how-video-game-consoles-make-mon.workingTitle: Why Console Makers Can Sell Hardware at a Loss
hbm-031-how-video-game-consoles-make-mon.centralHook: The console under your TV may have been sold at a loss. So where does the money come from?
hbm-031-how-video-game-consoles-make-mon.thesis: HYPOTHESIS: platform holders recover hardware losses through games, platform fees and subscriptions; segment reporting and public court filings document the economics.
hbm-031-how-video-game-consoles-make-mon.audience: US gamers 16-44; tech and business viewers
primarySources: Sony Group annual report (Game & Network Services segment)
Microsoft 10-K (gaming revenue)
Public filings from FTC v. Microsoft (testimony on console margins)
hbm-031-how-video-game-consoles-make-mon.factualRisk: Medium: per-unit loss figures only where a filing or sworn testimony states them
hbm-031-how-video-game-consoles-make-mon.visualPlan: Hardware vs software revenue stack, razor-and-blades diagram, subscription growth chart

hbm-022-how-subway-makes-money-on-sandwi.workingTitle: Who Really Pays for a Subway Restaurant?
hbm-022-how-subway-makes-money-on-sandwi.centralHook: Subway owns almost none of its restaurants. So who pays for them, and who gets paid?
hbm-022-how-subway-makes-money-on-sandwi.thesis: HYPOTHESIS: the franchisor earns royalties and advertising fees on franchisee sales while franchisees carry the costs; the exact fees are published in the Franchise Disclosure Document.
hbm-022-how-subway-makes-money-on-sandwi.audience: US adults; small-business and franchise-curious viewers
primarySources: Subway Franchise Disclosure Document (state filings, e.g. Wisconsin/California registries)
Company statements on restaurant counts
hbm-022-how-subway-makes-money-on-sandwi.factualRisk: Medium: fees and counts change by year; cite the FDD year
hbm-022-how-subway-makes-money-on-sandwi.visualPlan: Money-flow from one sandwich to franchisor/franchisee, FDD excerpts, store-count chart

hbm-101-how-sneakers-make-money-from-res.workingTitle: Why Sneaker Drops Are Designed to Sell Out
hbm-101-how-sneakers-make-money-from-res.centralHook: Some sneakers sell out in minutes and resell for far more. Who benefits from the shortage?
hbm-101-how-sneakers-make-money-from-res.thesis: HYPOTHESIS: limited releases build brand heat that supports full-price sales elsewhere, while resale platforms capture fees on the secondary market; brand filings and platform disclosures bound what can be said.
hbm-101-how-sneakers-make-money-from-res.audience: US sneaker fans 16-34; streetwear and resale viewers
primarySources: Nike 10-K (direct-to-consumer, demand creation)
Resale platform disclosures (fees; label private-company data as self-reported)
hbm-101-how-sneakers-make-money-from-res.factualRisk: High: resale-market sizes are often estimates; attribute every figure
hbm-101-how-sneakers-make-money-from-res.visualPlan: Release-day timeline, retail vs resale price comparison (dated), fee waterfall

hbm-037-how-airbnb-makes-money-when-host.workingTitle: Who Sets the Price on Airbnb, and Who Collects the Fees?
hbm-037-how-airbnb-makes-money-when-host.centralHook: The host sets the nightly rate. So why is the total at checkout so different?
hbm-037-how-airbnb-makes-money-when-host.thesis: HYPOTHESIS: the platform earns service fees from guests and/or hosts and a take rate on bookings, while hosts carry cleaning and pricing decisions; the 10-K documents the fee model and its changes.
hbm-037-how-airbnb-makes-money-when-host.audience: US travellers 25-54; hosts and would-be hosts
primarySources: Airbnb 10-K (revenue recognition, fee structure, take rate)
Airbnb fee-policy announcements (dated)
hbm-037-how-airbnb-makes-money-when-host.factualRisk: Low-Medium: fee rules changed over time; date every rule
hbm-037-how-airbnb-makes-money-when-host.visualPlan: Checkout receipt breakdown, money-flow host/guest/platform, policy timeline

hbm-046-how-sports-teams-make-money-even.workingTitle: The One NFL Team That Shows Its Books
hbm-046-how-sports-teams-make-money-even.centralHook: Most NFL teams never publish their finances. One does. What do its numbers say about losing seasons?
hbm-046-how-sports-teams-make-money-even.thesis: HYPOTHESIS: shared national revenue keeps team income steady regardless of results; the Green Bay Packers' published annual financials document the national revenue share.
primarySources: Green Bay Packers annual financial report (publicly released)
League statements on revenue sharing
hbm-046-how-sports-teams-make-money-even.factualRisk: Medium: one team's books cannot be generalised to all; say so
hbm-046-how-sports-teams-make-money-even.visualPlan: Revenue-source stack from the Packers report, win-loss vs revenue chart, revenue-sharing diagram

cs-047-how-ford-makes-more-from-trucks-t.centralHook: Ford sells cars, trucks and electric vehicles. Only some of them make money. Which?
cs-047-how-ford-makes-more-from-trucks-t.thesis: HYPOTHESIS: segment reporting shows where Ford's profits and losses sit (commercial and combustion businesses vs electric); the 10-K segments document it.
cs-047-how-ford-makes-more-from-trucks-t.audience: US adults 25-64; truck owners and auto fans
primarySources: Ford 10-K segment results (Ford Blue, Ford Model e, Ford Pro)
Ford earnings releases
cs-047-how-ford-makes-more-from-trucks-t.factualRisk: Low-Medium: segment definitions change; cite fiscal years
cs-047-how-ford-makes-more-from-trucks-t.visualPlan: Segment EBIT bars, product-mix chart, F-Series vs EV unit chart

pp-017-why-jcpenney-lost-customers-when-.workingTitle: The Year JCPenney Stopped Running Sales
pp-017-why-jcpenney-lost-customers-when-.centralHook: A retailer decided to stop running sales and simply charge fair prices. What happened next?
pp-017-why-jcpenney-lost-customers-when-.thesis: HYPOTHESIS: the end of constant promotions coincided with a sharp drop in sales; filings and earnings calls from that period document the decline and the reversal.
pp-017-why-jcpenney-lost-customers-when-.audience: US shoppers 25-64; marketing and pricing-psychology viewers
primarySources: J. C. Penney 10-K and earnings releases for the fiscal years around the pricing change
Company statements announcing and reversing the strategy
pp-017-why-jcpenney-lost-customers-when-.factualRisk: Medium: causation (pricing vs other factors) must stay as the filings frame it
pp-017-why-jcpenney-lost-customers-when-.visualPlan: Sales-trend chart, before/after price tag graphics, strategy timeline
